messages:
Maya R.: Heads up — pslot backlog just spiked in usw2 for gpt-medium. Queue depth ~18,200 and p99 token latency climbing.
Tariq: Got it. Any model mix change or traffic shift?
Maya R.: Not that I see from frontdoor logs. Traffic steady but we lost 2 worker pods in pool-3 around 17:02 UTC.
QueueMonitorBot: ALERT: region=usw2 model=gpt-medium queue_depth=18200 p50=42ms p95=1.8s p99=3.6s worker_down=2 fallback_capacity=8%
Zoe: Can we reduce admission weight for gpt-medium in usw2 and route lower-priority traffic to eu1 fallback?
Lucas: Agree. Suggested patch: `routing-policy: capacity-first` + `admission_control: model=gpt-medium region=usw2 weight=0.65` — will throttle new requests, keep retries to other regions.
ops-runner: Reminder: cross-region fallback increases egress cost. If we move ~15% traffic to eu1 we should estimate network egress and SLO impact.
Tariq: Quick check: can we spin up 1-2 spare GPUs in usw2 on dedicated to absorb burst? Estimated warmup ~3m.
Maya R.: Spinning a spare now (started job rtx-provision-1799). If provisioning fails fallback change will be applied.
Oncall: If queue >30k or p99 >8s page infra-oncall.
Zoe: I'll prepare the admit-change and a short runbook: 1) apply admission weight 0.65 2) enable eu1 fallback-route 3) monitor prefix cache hitrate 4) revert if p99 doesn't drop in 5m.
Maya R.: Applying step 1 now: `sh ./opsctl set-admission --model gpt-medium --region usw2 --weight 0.65`
QueueMonitorBot: ACTION: admission_control_change detected by maya at 1799994345.
Tariq: Seeing immediate drop in backlog to 11k — nice. p95 down to 1.2s.
ops-runner: Can someone add cost estimate to the ticket? Putting a note: potential eu1 egress charge ~ $0.03/token for routed traffic (estimate).
Zoe: Will add to ticket + link to deploy diff. If provisioning finishes we should revert admission weight back up.
Maya R.: Provision succeeded, 2 workers back in pool-3 at 1799994378. Rolling admission back to 0.9 now.
QueueMonitorBot: INFO: queue_depth=3200 p95=420ms p99=760ms workers_online=12
Oncall: Closing loop — no page. Filing postmortem if we hit >25% SLA impact.
Tariq: TL;DR — transient worker loss caused backlog; admission control + quick provisioning prevented SLA breach; cost tradeoff noted for cross-region fallback.
Maya R.: Filing brief incident note and tagging @product for visibility on model-level routing consequences. :white_check_mark:
